# v3.13

This stable release rolls up dev pre-releases **v3.08-dev … v3.13-dev**. It is a
security-hardening release: one change alters how pages behave in your browser,
and the rest tighten the parts of the system that run behind the scenes.

## The one change you might notice

**Stronger protection against injected scripts.** Training Tracker now tells
your browser to run *only* the scripts Training Tracker itself put on the page.
Anything else — a `<script>` block or an `onclick` that somehow found its way
into a page — is treated as plain text and does not run. This is the single
biggest protection against a whole class of web attack.

You should not see any difference. Every page, chart, report, export, the help
window and the colour picker were checked and behave exactly as before.

**If something does misbehave**, an administrator can restore the previous
behaviour immediately — no rebuild, just a setting and a restart:

```
echo 'CSP_MODE=legacy' >> /opt/training-tracker/.env
systemctl restart training-tracker
```

The setting survives future updates, so it stays in effect until removed. Full
instructions are under Troubleshooting in the README. Please do report it if you
need to use this — a page that requires the old behaviour is a bug worth fixing
properly rather than living with. A `report-only` setting also exists for
diagnosing *which* script is at fault; note that no policy is enforced at all
while it is on, so it is a short diagnostic window rather than a safer middle
setting.

This change covers scripts only. Styling is unaffected and the app looks
exactly as it did.

## Behind the scenes

- **The update and backup schedules are read far more defensively.** A damaged
  or tampered schedule file is now ignored — the job simply does not run that
  tick — instead of being able to leave a stuck background process behind every
  five minutes.

- **Update progress and log files are repaired in place** if their permissions
  have drifted, rather than being recreated. Their contents are kept, and the
  repair now works on container setups where it previously could not.

- **The updater checks the settings it reads from your configuration file
  before acting on them.** The certificate file it trusts must be one only an
  administrator can change. Everything else is reported but still used — in
  particular your database connection setting is always honoured, so the
  pre-update database backup and its rollback are never skipped.

- **Diagnostic crash reports** collected after a failed update are read in a way
  that cannot be redirected to an unrelated file.

- **Installing Node.js during a fresh install is skipped only when a suitable
  version is already installed system-wide**, so a host can no longer finish
  installing with a copy the service itself cannot reach. Otherwise the setup
  script is downloaded and checked before it is run.

- **Running the install or update script through `sudo` no longer carries your
  own environment into the administrator session.**

- **The check that guarantees every API endpoint asks who is calling is
  stricter.** The public API's global on/off switch was being accepted as
  though it were an identity check. No endpoint was ever affected — the gap was
  in the safety net, not the app.

- **Company scoping now fails safe in several shared reporting queries.** A
  caller scoped to *no* companies now reliably gets nothing rather than
  everything. Nothing in the app could reach the old behaviour, so no report or
  export has ever shown the wrong data; this removes the possibility for
  anything added later.

## Housekeeping

- Long-standing design decisions are now recorded in the code where they had
  started to look like oversights, and comments describing the partner-program
  dashboards now describe what each layout does rather than naming particular
  programs.

- Several pieces of contributor documentation were corrected to match what the
  system actually does.

## Upgrading

No action required. Updating promptly is recommended.
